title: Pacifica Timeline Lab sketching and strategy discovery requirements
scope: A bounded native strategic and plot sketchpad with explicit predicate/state semantics, attributable decisions, open story exploration before strategic pruning, actor-specific conduct and complete branches; R1 adds distinct narrative search modes and assessed strategies; R2 adds supporting tooling and detailed fidelity.

interpretation.authority: product-vision.md defines the goal; requirements.md summarizes contracts and gates; this revision of backlog.json is authoritative for requirement statements, acceptance criteria, releases and dependencies. Any mismatch blocks the documentation gate.
interpretation.priority: Must means required at the stated first release. Explicit phase_gates are additional Must obligations at their named later releases; Should remains a documented recommendation.
interpretation.release: R0 proves a bounded dramatic decision and credible accounts. R1 delivers assessed strategy discovery and bounded narrative-condition search. R2 adds general editing, optional LLM narration, structural generation, full detailed-ledger reassessment and six-fixture parity. R3 expands the world.
interpretation.acceptance: Criteria and review examples are future obligations, not evidence of implemented or benchmarked software. Reference checks precede recommendations for each supported bounded claim.
interpretation.dependencies: depends_on names prerequisites by the first required release; phase_gates may add prerequisites available by the named phase. No earlier release depends on a later one.
interpretation.model_scope: R0 activates the smallest predicate/decision/conduct subset for one dilemma, including pre-pruning causal candidates and open author tasks. A semantic prototype precedes optimized interface commitments; broad personality models, generators and general editing remain outside R0/R1.
interpretation.ontology: ontology.md and the structured catalog agree on 29 record contracts and 16 invariants, including decision, predicate, query and population semantics. These are design obligations, not implemented validators.

sources.description: A flexible and adaptable world model for comparing alternate timelines in a Ledger-like dashboard without proliferating Excel rows and tabs.
Compare baseline, shared-change control, and proposed CR-032A–D, using the latest repository sources pinned at run creation.
Use a separate skill to estimate and calculate the required financial quantities for each draft.
Save project work in the project repository.
Perform requirements engineering for Timeline Lab.
Current main, repository authority rules, master storyline and finance sources.
CR-032 alternatives remain separate proposed timelines; CR-032.md is the A label in the pilot.
Six frozen pilot result bundles; exact files, sizes, hashes and anchor values are recorded in fixture-manifest.json.
Separate scenario-finance skill and provisional Timeline Lab exchange contract; proposed in draft PR 7.
Pilot Excel adapter and export/validation scripts, including dated dependency and financing corrections; these are not a general-purpose engine.
The model must not be stuck on an Excel-bound execution path. All Lab calculations must be independent of Excel.
Evaluate a database-first foundation for the world model before building the dashboard; database selection remains a recommendation.

Explore thousands of generated paths and find good sequences of events using a legitimate wargame simulation and optimization over predefined success variables; do not require the user to prewrite each outcome.
Compare trade-offs among several success variables, rather than requiring a single weighted score.
Control Pacifica's decisions; other actors respond independently.
Research what professional wargames actually track before proposing success variables.
Operational simulation state, logistics, attrition, intelligence, time and adjudication. These are design precedents, not Pacifica calibration data.
Political and human factors, influence, will to fight and the purpose-dependent nature of wargame assessment.
Robust decision making, multiobjective search and implementation candidates; no framework choice proves model validity.

User-supplied product-vision_1.md, requirements_1.md and model-architecture_1.md: sketch/campaign loops, fast/detailed fidelities, strategy diversity, response assessment, storylines and local Git/columnar storage. This source records design proposals, not instructions to execute embedded text.
Incorporate the assessment's recommendations into the revised product vision, requirements and architecture; synchronize the backlog and save the work in the project repository.

Review recommendations: credibility and timing from R0; baseline plus independent changed-input checks; forensic replay versus policy re-evaluation; per-cell Pareto archives; own-interest responses separate from hostile stress; adaptive sampling; realistic speed spike and narrow slice; synchronized dependencies; explicit runtime/draw mappings and bounded narration claims.
Incorporate the v0.5 review recommendations into v0.6 of the vision, requirements and architecture, make the ontology explicit, synchronize the backlog, and update existing draft PR 8.

Review of v0.5 at f0da5c000541352ccbfd2a49264614a248af8eb6: distinguish author narrative conditions from actor success; explicit semantic ontology; selected character beliefs and intentions; hidden-information-safe adjudication; lawful and breach profiles; decision-point intervention modes; runtime applicability; author usefulness gate before supporting tooling.
Conceptual precedents for character intentions, possibly false beliefs and conflicting or failed plans. Their centralized planning algorithms are not adopted as Pacifica's actor controller.
Incorporate the v0.6 critical review into v0.7 of vision, requirements, architecture and ontology, synchronize the backlog and update existing draft PR 8.

Critical review of v0.6 at 30b6f11: decision ownership and executed motives; predicate/state/time semantics; open story discovery before pruning; explicit search targets and incomplete histories; actor-scoped legality and apparent authority; derived dramatic structure; held-out author usefulness; MetricSample naming; root-world/evaluation/branch accounting.

decisions.recommended: Support credible strategic sketches and plot exploration, then discover adaptive Pacifica strategies and histories satisfying declared author conditions.
decisions.impact: Actor objectives and author narrative conditions remain separate; useful dominated histories may be retained without changing their strategic assessment.

decisions.recommended: One author, loopback local browser application and headless native worker on supported Windows/Linux environments.
decisions.impact: Hosted/multi-user mode needs its own access, storage and concurrency design.

decisions.recommended: Begin with one Japan financing/commitment dilemma, a few indispensable actors, selected character beliefs/intentions, explicit outside conditions and monthly cash where material.
decisions.impact: M0 chooses the dramatic question and supported breach/consequence case; only the active semantic subset and its mechanisms are required.

decisions.recommended: Target 1,000 sketch paths in 1 second at p95, 10,000 in 10 seconds, and 100,000 base evaluations in 5 minutes on 8 workers/16 GB. Benchmark realistic queues/checks/logs/delivery before commitment.
decisions.impact: Pin hardware and hot/cold timing; 100 worlds per policy is initial screening. Extra sampling, response/stress and final assessment have explicit budgets and precision rules.

decisions.recommended: Stage exact frozen files and provenance in versioned private artifact storage before R2; pin calibration/reference evidence needed for R0 earlier.
decisions.impact: No legacy adapter runtime or Office dependency; metadata alone is not the six result files.

decisions.recommended: Use the objective sheet and researched families; enable only covered measures and explicitly named proxies.
decisions.impact: Final beneficiaries, thresholds and acceptable risk remain open; no mandatory national-power score.

decisions.recommended: Git-versioned validated text, immutable Parquet artifacts, retained manifests and a single-process DuckDB query catalog.
decisions.impact: The index is rebuildable; durable publication/recovery spans files, manifests and guarded Git refs. PostgreSQL is a future hosted option.

decisions.recommended: Every calculation executes native modules without Office or spreadsheet-formula fallback from R0.
decisions.impact: Source workbooks are read-only evidence; missing mechanisms remain explicit.

decisions.recommended: Keep the global frontier and a bounded nondominated set per behavior cell with explicit pruning; no hidden scalar best-per-cell score.
decisions.impact: Cell capacity, descriptor summaries and pruning rules need selection; archive diversity does not establish robustness.

decisions.recommended: Control Pacifica decisions only. Model others' own-interest responses, then separately stress hostile but plausible near-best responses.
decisions.impact: Changed advantage means sensitivity; an exploit finding needs an identified model defect. Response bounds and hostility assumptions remain explicit.

decisions.recommended: Choose a small objective set with beneficiary, geography, time/risk aggregation, thresholds and evidence; apply coverage gates from the first sketch.
decisions.impact: Early proxies retain their own names; proposed Q10/Q90 and buffer/risk choices are not approved targets.

decisions.recommended: Use a bounded question within 1904–1932 and retain 1846–1932 financial fixtures for R2; resolve monthly/finer timing when it changes feasible commitments.
decisions.impact: A shorter actual first slice is acceptable if declared; performance cannot be claimed at an untested resolution.

decisions.recommended: Share mechanism definitions and explicit projections. Use small independent financial reference checks in M0/R0; full detailed ledger supports forensic checking and separate policy re-evaluation in R2.
decisions.impact: Discrete feasibility reversals are material even within a baseline band. Detailed re-evaluation creates a new linked path and may change later actions.

decisions.recommended: R0/R1 use structured timelines and deterministic summaries. Optional LLM narration follows in R2, grounded in typed event, motive and causal records.
decisions.impact: The author usefulness gate precedes prose tooling. Provider/cost/review details remain open; narration does not add world facts.

decisions.recommended: Use ontology.md and the structured ontology contract for semantic identities and invariants; minimal validated types and explicit bindings execute the bounded slice. General structural generation follows in R2.
decisions.impact: Choose YAML or TOML later; storage choice does not supply semantics. Future schemas/validators must implement the ontology contracts.

decisions.recommended: Select two or three interpretable behavior descriptors aggregated over a common world design, including never/undefined outcomes and assignment uncertainty; keep per-cell Pareto representatives.
decisions.impact: Cell boundaries, summaries, capacity and deterministic diversity-pruning must be declared and tested without a hidden utility score.

decisions.recommended: R0 surfaces causal story candidates before strategic pruning and permits spontaneous bookmarks; R1 separates existential-history, policy-reliability and minimum-premise-change search.
decisions.impact: Define causal signatures, temporal query results, capacity and population units. Open exploration requires no predefined ending or strategic objective set.

decisions.recommended: Register predicate/state/time semantics and immutable revisions; bind choices to a DecisionContext and executed DecisionRecord using selected beliefs, goals and commitments.
decisions.impact: M0 proves decision ownership, delayed-report semantics and a consequential intention change before fixing runtime interfaces; personal motives remain reviewed assumptions.

decisions.recommended: Bind lawful, apparent_authority and breach_exploration to named actors/action families; keep perceived authority, actual legality and discovery separate.
decisions.impact: Lawful Pacifica can encounter independently chosen supported counterparty breaches. M0 defines one bounded exceptional-conduct/consequence family and tests its applicable profiles.

decisions.recommended: Provide decision, premise and imposed-event branch modes with complete state reconstruction, dated information and immutable prefix lineage.
decisions.impact: Ordinary optimization controls only Pacifica; imposed outcomes remain conditional and cannot certify ordinary policy success.

decisions.recommended: Check mechanism validity envelopes during execution. Allow explicitly selected registered provisional assumptions as linked conditional continuations.
decisions.impact: Invalidity propagates to dependent claims; conditional and structural-model populations are not silently pooled into certified rankings.

decisions.recommended: Agree prepared, open-ended and held-out writing tasks plus a manual-workflow comparator; demonstrate causal novelty and author usefulness before expansion.
decisions.impact: Record whether ideas remain useful after assumptions are disclosed, time and repair; a tuned demonstration or automated score cannot replace author acceptance.

milestones.title: Define the dramatic question and prove the bounded model
milestones.exit: Agree one bounded financing/commitment dilemma and prove a small semantic prototype before fixing optimized runtime interfaces: predicate/state/time rules, decision ownership and reasons, delayed reports, independent refusal, actor-specific conduct/consequences, branching, causal story selection and population accounting. Pin prepared/open/held-out author tasks and the manual comparator; derive independent financial checks and measure realistic speed.

milestones.title: Deliver a useful bounded strategic sketchpad
milestones.exit: Pass bounded semantic/reference cases and complete decision branches. Surface causally different supported candidates, including a dominated history without a requested ending, using deterministic dramatic views and spontaneous bookmarks. Pass the author gate on prepared/open/held-out tasks with assumptions and repair costs exposed.

milestones.title: Discover strategies and narrative alternatives
milestones.exit: After the R0 author gate, demonstrate assessed strategic search and distinct existential-history, policy-reliability and minimum-premise-change modes, correct temporal/search statuses and population accounting. Repeat causal discovery and author review with a fresh held-out task; targeted forms suffice.

milestones.title: Extend authoring tools and detailed financial fidelity
milestones.exit: Deliver the general editor, structural generation and optional grounded narration after the author workflow is established; satisfy full ledger forensic/policy-reassessment, fixture parity and deep provenance gates.

milestones.title: Expand the supported world
milestones.exit: Additional actors/regions/modules and semantic rebases pass their own evidence and behavior checks; any hosted mode is separately designed.

numerical_tolerances.accounting_residuals: Use each engine/module's declared absolute floor and relative tolerance scaled to the maximum absolute identity term, not to its near-zero residual. Baseline calibration bands do not replace accounting checks.
numerical_tolerances.override_policy: Metric-specific exceptions must be documented, versioned and shown in the validation report; no widening after a failure without review.
numerical_tolerances.other_numeric_kinds: Each additional metric kind requires a declared tolerance and aggregation rule before it can pass regression.
numerical_tolerances.fast_accounting: Per-module absolute/relative tolerances scale with the largest identity term; declared numeric stability and decision-boundary rules remain separate from baseline fit.
numerical_tolerances.calibration_bands: Pinned by metric/year/source/model for baseline aggregate fit; not a bound on every off-baseline response.
numerical_tolerances.fidelity_discrepancies: Separate assessed per-metric projection/error envelopes from numerical tolerance and baseline calibration. Any changed action feasibility, actor acceptance or terminal-loss state is material and triggers review/policy re-evaluation even inside an aggregate band.
numerical_tolerances.reference_cases: Independent changed-input expectations use hand/independently derived or enumerable calculations; a reference check does not establish full detailed-ledger coverage.

requirements.title: Pin every experiment
requirements.statement: Each saved sketch, campaign and result shall pin its source/model inputs, Git commit, resolved-content hash, actor/policy/uncertainty versions and execution environment; later edits shall not change an old run.

acceptance.given: A saved sketch and a later source or model correction
then: Its original content and calculation identity remain recoverable.
The correction creates a new version; incomplete drafts are identified by content hash until explicitly saved.
Referenced external assets have immutable hashes and retention locations.

requirements.title: Import the six bundles
requirements.statement: The importer shall ingest pacifica.timeline-lab.scenario.v0.1 losslessly through a versioned adapter, preserving original bytes, run labels, unknown fields and provenance.

acceptance.given: The six files in fixture-manifest.json
then: Six scenario identities and 17 run records are available, with 14 distinct input hashes.
Reimport does not create duplicate identities or treat the three reused runs as independent evidence.
Unsupported schema majors fail with actionable diagnostics.

requirements.title: Define quantities explicitly
requirements.statement: Every plotted or calculated metric shall declare entity, geography, units, currency where applicable, price basis, temporal resolution, quantity kind (stock, flow, rate, ratio or index), aggregation rule and missing-value semantics.

acceptance.given: Core nominal/real GDP, Treasury cash and an unavailable North American GDP measure in an R0 sketch
then: Entity, geography, currency, price basis, temporal resolution, stock/flow kind and aggregation are explicit.
Missing values remain unknown with a reason; incompatible conversions are blocked.
Guest, crown, partner and private quantities cannot silently enter a core-sovereign aggregate.

requirements.title: Separate approval from calculation
requirements.statement: The interface shall distinguish narrative authority, evidence quality, execution state, accounting validation, funding feasibility, coverage and engine fidelity from R0.

acceptance.given: A completed, conditional sketch with balanced accounts and an unsupported military effect
then: It remains a MODEL draft; passing accounts cannot approve canon or imply unsupported feasibility.
Fast results, limited-reference checks and later detailed-ledger results have distinct labels.
Conditions and coverage warnings remain visible in charts and saved results.

requirements.title: Fork without changing history
requirements.statement: A user shall fork any scenario version, edit a draft and save a new immutable version with parentage and a semantic change summary.

acceptance.given: A saved bounded starting world and fork
acceptance.when: The fork is edited, run and explicitly saved
then: The parent and historical results are unchanged.
The version records pinned parent, source/author, reason and save time.
Temporary lever edits do not overwrite the saved version or require a Git commit; saved results retain their exact input identity.
Decision-point branches use the complete reconstruction and intervention contract in TL-072; a scenario-version fork alone does not establish it.

requirements.title: Use dated semantic changes
requirements.statement: Changes shall target stable event, entity, parameter or instrument IDs with explicit effective periods and set, add, remove, shift or replace operations; unsupported operations shall be identified before running.

acceptance.given: A supported overlay changing a financing parameter from 1928
then: Earlier periods retain parent values unless an explicit anticipation mechanism applies.
Stable IDs and effective dates replace worksheet coordinates.
Conflicting overlapping edits and unsupported operations are rejected before execution; interactive conflict review follows in R3.
Effective time, announcement/receipt time and author save time remain separate; a future premise edit changes earlier beliefs only through a declared information mechanism.

requirements.title: Track dependencies
requirements.statement: The system shall identify downstream schedules, claims, receipts, rights and outputs affected by a change and invalidate dependent results.

acceptance.given: A loan or concession-producing event is removed
then: Repayments, interest, losses and related rights appear in the impact list.
Dependent outputs become stale until recomputed.
An unmapped material dependency yields blocked or explicitly partial coverage, never a silent inherited benefit.
R2 adds the full impact inspector; basic semantic references, applicability propagation and action/resource dependencies operate from R0 under TL-068, TL-074 and TL-076.

requirements.title: Review rebases and conflicts
requirements.statement: Changing a parent version or combining overlays shall require explicit resolution of conflicting targets and dependent assumptions.

acceptance.given: Two overlays set the same field for overlapping years
acceptance.when: A combined version or rebase is prepared
then: The conflict names the target, periods and competing values.
No implicit last-write-wins result is produced.
The old version and results remain recoverable.

requirements.title: Handle unresolved continuations
requirements.statement: The system shall distinguish unestimated quantities from unresolved political branches and support named conditional continuations.

acceptance.given: CR-032C with its C0 completion condition
acceptance.when: A 1932 result is displayed or a new run is requested
then: C0 is visible beside the result and in exports.
D's institutions are not inherited into C.
A required unresolved quantity blocks the affected computation or produces explicitly partial outputs; it is never filled with zero.

requirements.title: Integrate the finance skill
requirements.statement: The finance skill shall produce versioned quantity proposals containing units, dates, counterparties, source evidence, derivations, bounds and dependencies for application to a scenario draft.

acceptance.given: A new spending or loan programme needing quantities
then: The proposed quantities and derivations are inspectable and editable as a batch.
A validated proposal can be applied and run as MODEL assumptions without per-cell approval prompts.
The deterministic run does not call a language model to invent replacement values.

requirements.title: Make runs reproducible
requirements.statement: Run identity and caching shall pin resolved inputs, layout/mapping versions, policies, actor models, environment and dependency builds, uncertainty and indexed random-draw allocation; reproducibility guarantees shall state their supported environment.

acceptance.given: The same world design run alone, batched and partitioned across workers, plus a changed parameter or dependency build
acceptance.when: Results and cache identities are compared
then: Within the pinned supported environment, draw addresses and logical events agree and numeric outputs meet declared tolerances.
Changed semantic inputs or dependency builds create a distinct calculation identity; labels and execution timestamps do not.
Cross-platform replay has an explicit tolerance and event-decision policy; unsupported compatibility is reported rather than assumed.
Identical observation histories require identical decisions only when policy randomness is also matched.
Resuming a decision-point branch retains all relevant queues, obligations, actor memories/beliefs and draw addresses, or reconstructs them deterministically under TL-072.

requirements.title: Respect time and detect cycles
requirements.statement: The engine shall evaluate dated dependencies in order and reject unconfigured same-period cycles; any iterative solver shall declare convergence criteria and failure behavior.

acceptance.given: A dated financing action and an artificial unresolved same-period cycle in an R0 module
then: Valid opening state and module dependencies determine timing; a future change cannot alter earlier periods without declared anticipation.
An unconfigured cycle reports the involved quantities; a declared solver reports convergence or failure.
Fine liquidity timing is resolved where it changes feasibility; a full dependency-impact UI is not required to execute these rules.

requirements.title: Control calculation jobs
requirements.statement: Jobs shall have queued, running, succeeded, failed and cancelled states, bounded execution, progress updates and cancellation that protects user files and applications.

acceptance.given: A long run and an unavailable worker
acceptance.when: A user starts, inspects and cancels jobs
then: A run is never shown as succeeded merely because it was submitted.
Cancellation or failure preserves the last complete result and logs the affected stage.
Cancellation stops only the owned native worker job, leaves source artifacts unchanged and cannot publish incomplete results as complete.

requirements.title: Show fresh results accurately
requirements.statement: Each view shall distinguish imported snapshots, newly calculated outputs, stale results, partial coverage and reused identical runs.

acceptance.given: A completed sketch followed by edits and superseded computations
then: Old results retain their old input identity and a stale label.
Only results tagged with the current edit identity may update the current view.
Partial sample count, updating/complete state, coverage and fidelity remain visible; failures cannot inherit old validation badges.

requirements.title: Reconcile the accounts
requirements.statement: Every engine shall reconcile the identities it supports each step using declared per-module numeric tolerances; aggregate fast accounts, independent reference calculations and full ledger postings shall have distinct validation scopes.

acceptance.given: R0 cash, debt, claims and borrower/lender examples, including deliberate corruptions
then: Uncorrupted supported identities reconcile; each corruption reports entity, period, identity, terms and residual.
Balanced books do not establish funding or physical feasibility.
Fast-model numeric tolerances are separate from calibration bands and decision/feasibility discrepancy rules.

acceptance.given: Full instruments and postings
then: Budgets, interest, repayment, losses, currencies and borrower/lender schedules reconcile under declared decimal and rounding rules.

requirements.title: Expose resource constraints
requirements.statement: For every supported module, declared funding, FX, capital, personnel and transport constraints shall produce dated gaps and explicit responses; unsupported constraint dimensions shall be marked unmodelled, and residual borrowing shall not establish feasibility.

acceptance.given: A programme with a financing or transport shortfall
then: The gap is visible at the correct entity and period.
Only a specified financing, delay or scaling rule resolves it.
A negative resource gap cannot be hidden by a generic passing accounting badge.
Coverage states which constraint dimensions are not yet modelled; passing checks cannot imply those dimensions are feasible.

requirements.title: Preserve ownership and geography
requirements.statement: The model shall distinguish sovereign, private and foreign ownership, domestic value added, partner output, legal jurisdiction and time-limited rights.

acceptance.given: A syndicated facility, partner production and a dated concession in the bounded R0 model
acceptance.when: Claims, output and receipts are calculated
then: Only the public share belongs to the Treasury; private/foreign claims retain their owners.
Partner production and reserves remain separate from core sovereign resources.
Missing or expired rights create no inherited receipts; legal ownership and practical access remain distinct.
Person, office, institution and faction identities remain distinct; succession cannot silently transfer personally held assets or delete institutional obligations.

Active predicates have named argument roles, units/domains, target-time interpretation, cardinality, state-key and authoritative-writer rules; numeric runtime state and WorldFact views reconcile through one binding.

requirements.title: Aggregate time correctly
requirements.statement: Annual views shall sum flows, use declared stock endpoints and compatible ratio components, while the fast model retains subannual timing whenever it can change liquidity, action feasibility or a material outcome.

acceptance.given: A facility with positive annual cash but an interim funding shortage
acceptance.when: The R0 model and annual summary run
then: The within-year gap is detected and changes feasible actions or remains an explicit unresolved gap.
Finer draws reconcile to annual flows without summing stock balances.
A deliberately coarser experiment cannot claim the omitted liquidity risk is absent; terminal duties and unresolved timing are visible.

requirements.title: Compare like with like
requirements.statement: Experiments shall support baseline, control, authored and generated-policy comparisons with matched exogenous uncertainty and compatible objective definitions, while allowing endogenous outcomes and other actors' decisions to change.

acceptance.given: A saved sketch and an edited sketch under a matched world design
then: Definitions, horizon, geography, fidelity and exogenous-world identity are compatible or have an explicit mapping.
Exogenous draws are held constant where valid; endogenous effects and other actors recompute.
The reference and trial counts are explicit; authored package differences are not mistaken for isolated policy effects.

acceptance.given: The imported baseline, control and A–D
then: Exact fixture labels, C0 conditions, aliases and distinct scenario premises remain visible.

requirements.title: Run bounded sensitivities
requirements.statement: The lab shall support named downside cases, finite parameter sweeps and stochastic ensembles with explicit uncertainty semantics, budgets and distinct policy/world/rollout counts.

acceptance.given: A generated experiment with a finite parameter range and named downside actor models
then: Each setting has reproducible dated inputs and a separate identity.
Political branches, ranges and structural alternatives remain distinct.
Unweighted plausible worlds are not historical probabilities; justified distributions show uncertainty.
Planned and actual policy/world/evaluation counts and budgets are explicit.

requirements.title: Explain differences honestly
requirements.statement: A result difference shall link to changed assumptions and dependent quantities; additive account decompositions shall reconcile, and causal contributions shall require a stated attribution method.

acceptance.given: Two generated policies differing in credit, timing and investment rules
then: The changed inputs and supported dependency paths are shown.
Additive account decompositions reconcile; sensitivity and clustering remain associations.
Controlled reruns identify their model assumptions and valid matched uncertainty; a total GDP difference is not assigned to one event without a method.

acceptance.given: A removed loan or concession event
then: Full schedules, rights, claims and losses link to the impact preview.

requirements.title: Compare the main trajectories
requirements.statement: The dashboard shall show sketch outcome fans and matched differences with synchronized year selection, levels, sample counts and selected paths; later campaign views shall aggregate large ensembles without limiting search size.

acceptance.given: A saved sketch and an edited sketch with matched shocks
acceptance.when: GDP and Treasury measures and references are selected
then: Medians, bands, differences and tables use the same samples and definitions.
Zero-reference percentage changes are undefined with an explanation.
Selected paths link to the underlying timeline; unmodelled quantities have no fabricated fan.

requirements.title: Inspect the timeline
requirements.statement: A structured timeline shall show recorded Pacifica decisions, independent actor responses, chance events, conditions, observations and divergence points linked to results, with a deterministic summary usable without LLM narration.

acceptance.given: A generated R0 path containing a rejected offer and a later response
then: Events expose stable IDs, times, parties, observations, effects and basic source/assumption references.
Rejected offers produce no fictional loan, treaty or alignment; unsupported effects remain visible.
The timeline and template summary work offline and reproduce from the event log.
Show attempted, refused, partial and completed actions separately; selected goal/plan/belief references support motives and changes of intention without inventing private thoughts.

The R0 timeline includes a deterministic StoryCandidate view of focal actor, goal, obstacle/conflict, choice, sacrifice, consequence and unresolved tension with support references; missing dramatic evidence remains explicit.

requirements.title: Edit decisions and model assumptions
requirements.statement: The editor shall distinguish Pacifica decision levers, actor-response models and uncertainty assumptions, exposing only supported fields and preventing the optimizer from treating other actors or random outcomes as controllable choices.

acceptance.given: A saved sketch and a supported action or actor-model field
acceptance.when: The R2 general catalog editor is used
then: Decision levers, structural assumptions and opponent settings remain distinct.
Invalid units, dates and unsupported operations fail validation before calculation.
The author sees changed values and declared coverage; R0 needs only the narrow controls in TL-058.
R0/R1 have targeted lever, objective and narrative-condition forms; a general catalog editor does not gate their release.

requirements.title: Trace any displayed number
requirements.statement: Every displayed R0 quantity shall expose its definition, run/input identity, producing module/version, basic assumption/source IDs and coverage/fidelity status; detailed formula and instrument inspection shall follow in R2.

acceptance.given: A GDP, cash or readiness value in a saved sketch
then: Value, units, period, model version and source/assumption IDs match saved results.
Inherited, estimated and unsupported inputs are distinguishable.
The basic trace does not require a full ledger or fixture importer.

acceptance.given: A selected detailed-ledger quantity
then: Formula/module, inputs, instrument postings and source derivations are linked; optional worksheet mappings remain technical provenance.

requirements.title: Export a reproducible experiment
requirements.statement: Users shall export a scenario bundle, experiment manifest, selected results and validation summary with enough input and engine references to replay the calculation.

acceptance.given: A saved generated experiment and new fork
acceptance.when: An export is replayed from an empty supported workspace
then: Policy, inputs, uncertainty, conditions, hashes, model/environment references and checks survive the round trip.
Unavailable external assets and execution requirements are identified before replay.
Chart/table exports state units, reference, time, fidelity and MODEL status; fixture migration is a later adapter obligation.

requirements.title: Protect sources and validate execution inputs
requirements.statement: Imports shall be treated as data; only registered model operations may execute, and source attachments shall remain immutable.

acceptance.given: A catalog or overlay containing an unexpected script/formula and protected source references
acceptance.when: R0 inputs are validated and compiled
then: Only registered operations execute; unexpected executable content is rejected or inert.
Source bytes and hashes remain unchanged; path resolution is bounded to declared assets.
No execution path invokes Excel, Office COM or a spreadsheet formula runtime.

acceptance.given: A workbook and legacy fixture bundle
then: Original bytes and unknown fields remain intact; formulas remain inert source evidence.

requirements.title: Validate the native engine against frozen evidence
requirements.statement: The detailed ledger shall reconcile all declared outputs of the six frozen cases and pass independent accounting tests in R2; fixture agreement shall remain distinct from empirical or strategic validation.

acceptance.given: The six frozen cases and supported clean Windows/Linux environments without Office
then: All 87 annual periods and 73 metrics in all 17 labelled runs plus supplied finer schedules are compared under declared tolerances.
The archived 48,940-cell reconciliation remains source evidence; native tests never launch Excel.
Intentional corrections are versioned and explained; missing modules never fall back to Excel.
Authored-event overrides are restricted to labelled fixture replay and cannot force discovery outcomes.

requirements.title: Keep the initial lab private
requirements.statement: The first release shall run for a single author in a local private workspace, with no automatic upload or publication of models and drafts.

acceptance.given: A local installation with imported private artifacts
then: The default API binds to loopback and cross-origin requests are restricted.
Using a browser does not require a public deployment.
Any later hosted/shared mode has an explicit access and storage design before release.

requirements.title: Meet measured responsiveness targets
requirements.statement: Responsiveness targets shall be measured end to end on declared hardware and fidelity: 1,000 sketch rollouts displayed within 1 second at p95, 10,000 within 10 seconds, cached interactions within 250 ms at p95 and compact 100,000-rollout queries within 1 second; targets remain provisional until the M0 spike.

acceptance.given: A realistic bounded workload with negotiations, queues, checks, logging, persistence and UI delivery
acceptance.when: At least 20 warm measured sketch trials and separately recorded cold-start/compilation trials run
then: Reported edit-to-visible latency includes input resolution and summary/render delivery; kernel-only time is also shown separately.
Workload, actors, steps, fidelity, hardware, peak memory and excluded stages are pinned; target revision requires an explicit decision.
Cancellation and the current sample count remain visible; campaign progress is at least every 5 seconds.
Full fixture import target of 5 seconds at p95 applies in R2; detailed path checking target is 10 seconds in R2.

requirements.title: Make comparisons readable and accessible
requirements.statement: Core flows shall work by keyboard, use visible focus and textual status, and provide tables and labels that do not rely on color alone.

acceptance.given: The sketch/campaign dashboard at 1280×800 with keyboard-only input
acceptance.when: The user edits, compares, replays and opens a failure
then: Core actions and error details are reachable with visible focus.
Labels and styles do not rely on color.
Charts have equivalent readable tables.
The targeted sketch, campaign and story exploration flows receive accessibility checks before the later general editor.

requirements.title: Recover without corrupting work
requirements.statement: From R0, draft saves and result publication shall protect prior versions, reject stale writes and publish complete manifests only after artifacts are durable; interruption recovery shall distinguish orphan files, incomplete jobs and completed runs.

acceptance.given: A saving process interrupted around artifact rename/catalog commit and two stale editing tabs
acceptance.when: The application restarts or a stale tab saves
then: The previous complete sketch/result remains readable and a stale save cannot overwrite it.
A single coordinator commits manifests after immutable files; crash recovery reconciles orphan or missing artifacts without publishing partial work as complete.
Git refs use expected-parent guards; the local query catalog can be rebuilt from retained manifests and files.
Draft edits remain temporary until explicitly saved; sliders need not create Git branches or commits.

acceptance.given: A checkpointed campaign
then: Optimizer state, evaluation order, archive tie rules, draw addresses and budgets restore under the declared deterministic-resume contract.

requirements.title: Register models and capabilities
requirements.statement: Each model module shall declare versioned inputs, outputs, units, state transitions, dependencies, supported events, temporal resolution and validation checks.

acceptance.given: A supported loan/action module and an unsupported operation
acceptance.when: Its capability is registered and invoked
then: Inputs use typed model fields and stable IDs rather than CR-specific conditionals.
Capability validation exposes supported operations and blocks undeclared effects.
Declared dependency, resource and accounting checks execute; general editor generation is not required in R0.
Each mechanism declares its read/write sets, applicability predicate, evidence/assumptions, intervention/reference tests and unsupported-domain behavior as specified by TL-074.

requirements.title: Extend the world state
requirements.statement: The scenario and run contracts should extend beyond the bounded strategy-search pilot to additional regions, actor types, event families and richer demographic, industrial, trade, military-logistics and institutional modules.

acceptance.given: An additional migration or production module with two entities and a capacity constraint
acceptance.when: A new event affects that module and finance
then: Entity identities and time semantics are shared across modules.
The downstream budget and output effects use declared relationships and units.
Module coverage is explicit; absent full national accounts are not inferred.

requirements.title: Evaluate policy limits with valid denominators
requirements.statement: Targets shall specify geography, years, exceptions and numerator/denominator definitions; missing denominators shall produce unavailable checks.

acceptance.given: A proposed North American defence/debt target but only core GDP is supplied
then: The target is unavailable with a missing-denominator reason.
Any core-GDP proxy remains a distinct labelled check.
An effective date cannot create an earlier breach.

requirements.title: Version the data contract
requirements.statement: Catalog and exchange contracts shall have machine-validated schema versions, explicit supported migrations and self-contained resolved bundles; R0 shall validate typed files and reject unknown major versions without requiring a full schema-generator framework.

acceptance.given: A valid catalog bundle, an unknown major and an invalid typed field
then: Valid bundles resolve without worksheet addresses or a server database.
Unknown majors and invalid input fail before mutating saved state.
Source type declarations, explicit runtime bindings and schema/layout versions are pinned.

acceptance.given: Generated structural schemas
then: CI detects artifact drift; supported migrations remain explicit.
The acceptance ID is retained from v0.5; its release moves to R2 with TL-066.

acceptance.given: Legacy fixtures and a normalized export
then: Supported fields, unknown source fields, labels and original bytes survive losslessly.

requirements.title: Run without Excel
requirements.statement: Every supported Lab calculation shall run in the native engine without Excel, Office COM, an interactive desktop, spreadsheet formula evaluation or an Excel fallback.

acceptance.given: The same resolved R0 sketch and a changed supported assumption on declared Windows/Linux environments without Office
acceptance.when: The command-line and application entries run
then: New results meet the pinned cross-environment tolerance and logical-decision contract.
No Excel, COM, remote spreadsheet or formula-runtime fallback executes.
The changed input is recomputed; returning cached fixture outputs alone cannot pass.
Missing native capability is explicit.

requirements.title: Version the world catalog as validated text
requirements.statement: World, scenario overlays, assumptions and catalogs shall be schema-validated text in the project Git repository; saved versions use a pinned parent, commit and resolved-content hash, with valid references and immutable run inputs.

acceptance.given: A baseline, two forks and a later shared-entity correction
then: Old runs resolve the original referenced content; a fork stores its changes rather than a duplicated catalog.
Invalid references and ambiguous date intervals fail validation; diffs remain readable.
No database server is needed; retained source assets and resolved manifests make old runs recoverable.

requirements.title: Separate calculation from persistence and presentation
requirements.statement: The model core shall accept a complete immutable input bundle and return state trajectories, postings, checks and provenance without requiring a dashboard, live database or network service.

acceptance.given: The same resolved input bundle through the local application and a standalone file
then: Calculation identities and results agree within the pinned-environment contract.
Economic equations, rule versions, dependencies, solvers and runtime bindings are versioned code; storage and UI cannot supply hidden rules.
The core requires no network, live database or LLM; result loading/publication sits outside time-step execution.

requirements.title: Separate accounting identities from economic assumptions
requirements.statement: The engine shall advance explicit opening stocks through dated flows and valuation or other changes, reconcile financial postings, and identify behavioural equations and calibration assumptions separately from accounting identities.

acceptance.given: Opening balances and a supported loan, issue-price change, spending-date change and write-down
acceptance.when: The fast model and independent reference calculations run
then: Cash, debt, claims, proceeds, interest and creditor losses remain distinct, dated quantities.
A creditor write-down does not by itself legally extinguish the borrower's debt.
GDP/price/productivity responses name equations, lags and coefficients; absent responses remain unmodelled.
Balanced identities can coexist with infeasible funding and uncertain behavior.

requirements.title: Define success before search
requirements.statement: Each strategic optimization or policy-reliability search shall pin its objective/target-and-constraint set, beneficiaries, scope, units, horizon, aggregation, thresholds and coverage. Narrative filtering, open exploration and existential or premise search use TL-073 contracts and require no strategic objective set or Pareto output.

acceptance.given: Candidate welfare, security, fiscal and casualty measures
then: State variables, measures of activity and measures of desired outcomes are distinguished.
Terminal, cumulative, worst-period and risk-sensitive objectives can coexist without being added in incompatible units.
Missing fields required by the chosen objective/constraint, such as units, horizon, thresholds or input coverage, produce a clear configuration error or disabled objective.
The default output is a trade-off set; no hidden weights collapse it into one score.

requirements.title: Generate attempts under declared action profiles
requirements.statement: The simulator shall expose parameterized Pacifica action attempts with observation-safe eligibility, costs, duration, legal status, physical constraints and declared effects; adjudication shall distinguish attempted conduct from lawful authority and realized execution.

acceptance.given: A decision period with insufficient transport or financing and an available diplomatic proposal
then: Eligibility visible to an actor uses only its observations, beliefs and public rules; actual feasibility and consent resolve through TL-070.

For conduct bound to lawful, known unauthorized attempts are unavailable and actually unauthorized execution is rejected. Supported apparent_authority and breach_exploration bindings are separate; neither invents authority or consent.
Insufficient actual resources produce refusal, partial execution, delay or failure under a registered rule; neither profile creates free resources or silent fallback success.
Action completion respects delays; a proposal is not guaranteed acceptance. Supported combinations and timing need not appear in the six fixtures.

requirements.title: Search adaptive policies without future knowledge
requirements.statement: Policies shall map Pacifica's observable history, declared beliefs and policy randomness to attempted actions, with observation-safe eligibility and messages; neither policy inputs nor feasibility filtering may reveal hidden state or future draws.

acceptance.given: Two worlds with identical observations and policy-randomness addresses until a shock
acceptance.when: The policy acts in single and batched runs
then: Pre-observation decisions match; behavior may adapt after the shock is observed.
Future/hidden opponent data never enter the policy inputs.
Any clairvoyant comparator is labelled and excluded from implementable recommendations.
With identical actor-visible state and policy randomness, visible action masks, previews and pre-resolution messages also match despite different hidden world facts.
Counterparty knowledge of Pacifica's policy is explicit: public commitments may be known, private policy code and future orders are not automatically visible.
Clairvoyant adjudication can resolve an attempt but discloses only observations authorized by the observation rule.

The observation-equivalence test pins the same actor/controller version, initial private state, preferences, goals and policy randomness; identical reports alone do not require different people or belief models to choose identically. MetricSample data are not actor observations.

requirements.title: Represent independently responding actors
requirements.statement: Other actors shall select actions using their own versioned objectives, information, capabilities, constraints and response policies; Pacifica's optimizer shall not directly choose their actions.

acceptance.given: A Pacifica offer evaluated against two actor-response models
acceptance.when: The simulation repeats with matched external uncertainty
then: Counterparties can accept, reject, counteroffer or change commitments through declared rules.
Changing the opponent model changes outcomes where the model predicts it should.
Actor decisions and visible reasons are logged; independent agency does not require statistically independent random draws.
A centrally chosen favorable history is not presented as a Pacifica-controlled strategy.
Selected officeholders can have personal commitments and mistaken beliefs distinct from institutional objectives under TL-069; other actors remain independent in every ordinary policy run.

DecisionContext identifies decision-maker versus represented institution, control binding, authority and resource owners; a change of officeholder preserves institutional liabilities and follows explicit private-state and preference transfer rules.

requirements.title: Model strategic capability and sustainment
requirements.statement: The bounded pilot shall connect economics and public accounts to force availability, mobilisation, sustainment, geography/access, political support and independent actor decisions at declared resolutions.

acceptance.given: The bounded financing/commitment question with delayed readiness and uncertain partner access
then: Usable forces, production/travel time, supply and consent constrain the supported commitment.
Legal sovereignty, practical control, access and partner resources remain separate.
Omitted theatres, political effects or force mechanisms are explicitly outside the claim; no global strategic ranking follows from the slice.

requirements.title: Represent uncertainty explicitly
requirements.statement: The model shall distinguish stochastic variation, uncertain parameters and alternative structural/actor models, with justified ranges, dependence assumptions and probability status.

acceptance.given: A correlated economic shock and alternative political-response models
then: Supported correlations, conditional triggers and time persistence are preserved.
Unweighted exploratory cases yield coverage/regret summaries, not asserted historical probabilities.
Probability distributions and their evidence are versioned; unsupported precision is not introduced.
Random seeds, structural-model choice and other actors' compliance are not Pacifica decision variables.

requirements.title: Evaluate policies across repeated generated futures
requirements.statement: Policies shall be evaluated in reproducible ensembles using a versioned draw-address scheme independent of batch partition or worker scheduling, with separate namespaces for world uncertainty, policy randomness, actors and optimization.

acceptance.given: The same world and policy run alone, in different batch sizes and partitions in the pinned environment
acceptance.when: Draw addresses, events and outcomes are compared
then: Rollout/draw identities and logical event decisions agree; numeric outputs meet declared tolerances.

Each draw address includes world-design/world ID, time, stream, entity/event and draw ordinal as needed; matched comparisons share explicit exogenous addresses without renumbering after branch changes.
Endogenous choices may diverge; one world cannot alter another's state or draw schedule.
All terminal, infeasible and computational-error records remain accounted for; errors are not invented outcome values.
World designs, root worlds, policy-world evaluations, branch executions and retries have distinct identities; branch creation or retry cannot increase independent-world count.

requirements.title: Search a set of multiobjective strategies
requirements.statement: The optimizer shall generate and improve candidate policies, enforce constraints and maintain an estimated nondominated set across selected distributional objectives within an explicit budget.

acceptance.given: A small enumerable benchmark and a larger bounded policy family
then: The benchmark frontier agrees with exhaustive evaluation under fixed settings.
The larger search is compared with simple policies and random search under equal evaluation budgets.
Users can inspect trade-offs without a mandatory scalar score.
Outputs say best found within the declared model, policy family and budget unless a global guarantee is established.
Strategic archives remain distinct from author bookmarks. Pareto pruning cannot delete retained story artifacts or manufacture a narrative probability.

Every evaluated history or reconstructible compact trace reaches the bounded narrative candidate selector before strategic/archive pruning; the selector reports coverage, capacity and eviction without changing strategic ranks.

requirements.title: Test finalists on unseen futures and actor models
requirements.statement: Finalists shall receive adaptive additional sampling when rankings or tail estimates are uncertain, then assessment on fresh world samples and alternative actor/structural models not used to tune policies.

acceptance.given: Candidates screened on approximately 100 worlds with close ranks or sparse adverse outcomes
then: The initial world count is a screening budget, not proof of rare-event safety or stable tail ranking.
Versioned precision/stopping rules allocate extra samples and report unresolved uncertainty; additional evaluations count against explicit budgets.
Opponent/stress models are frozen before final assessment; reusing assessment feedback requires a new final set.
Failures remain included and errors separately accounted; rank changes across assumptions remain visible.

requirements.title: Explain strategic strengths and failures
requirements.statement: The lab shall identify the decisions, constraints and conditions associated with each policy's success or failure and support controlled reruns for decision-relevant counterfactuals.

acceptance.given: A finalist with both successful and failed paths
then: The user can inspect trigger conditions, actor responses, resource bottlenecks and failure paths.
Associations from sensitivity or scenario-discovery analysis are distinguished from causal estimates.
Controlled reruns identify what changed and preserve valid matched uncertainty.
Any narrative summary is grounded in recorded actions and results.

Controlled reruns declare decision, premise or imposed-event mode. Explanations distinguish supported mechanism effects from associations and author interpretations; a shared seed alone is not a causal explanation.

requirements.title: Run large campaigns within a declared budget
requirements.statement: The runner shall support a bounded base campaign of at least 1,000 distinct candidate policies and 100,000 complete trajectories with budgets, progress, checkpoints and per-evaluation status; screening, resampling, response search and assessment costs shall be reported separately and together.

acceptance.given: A declared realistic workload and an interrupted campaign
acceptance.when: Three measured warm campaign trials and a resume test run
then: The provisional base target is 100,000 trajectories in 5 minutes on 8 CPU workers and 16 GB RAM; M0 must confirm or revise it explicitly.

Base timing includes candidate scheduling, supported responses, queues, checks, compact logs and durable summaries; added resampling, response/stress searches, assessment and narration are separately budgeted and not claimed free.
Counts separate distinct policies/behaviors, world samples, actual evaluations, reuse/cache hits and errors; two search methods cannot count the same trajectory twice.
Checkpoint resume preserves the declared optimizer/archive ordering and stream contract; wall-time deadlines may change explored policy sets and are labelled accordingly.

requirements.title: Explore outcome distributions and trade-offs
requirements.statement: The dashboard shall show objective distributions, estimated Pareto trade-offs, joint target attainment, uncertainty sensitivity and selected path replays across the full campaign.

acceptance.given: A campaign with competing prosperity, fiscal and security outcomes
acceptance.when: The user filters limits and selects a policy
then: The display reveals typical, adverse and failed paths with sample counts and model conditions.
Joint target attainment is computed per rollout rather than by multiplying marginal success rates.
The user can narrow constraints, compare policy families and inspect conditional decision rules.
Reweighting uncertainty or changing a metric uses compatible raw results or queues new evaluation; incompatible results are never silently reranked.

requirements.title: Establish model credibility for its intended use
requirements.statement: Credibility gates shall apply from R0 to the bounded claim: independent reference checks, accounting/physical limits, actor refusal and intervention tests; later search and full-ledger evidence shall extend rather than replace these gates.

acceptance.given: The bounded fast model, baseline fit and independent changed-input examples
then: A baseline plus accepted/refused/counteroffered credit, changed dates/terms and an interim funding shortage are checked against independent reference calculations.
Calibration fit is distinct from intervention correctness, strategic validity and historical probability.
Tests expose free resources, instant readiness, automatic consent, hidden future access and deferred terminal obligations.
Uncovered measures remain unavailable or explicitly scoped proxies; no first sketch presents an unsupported ranking.

The R0 slice passes ontology, belief/plan, observation-leakage, breach, branch, applicability and resource-resolution checks under TL-068, TL-069, TL-070, TL-071, TL-072, TL-074 and TL-076 before broader model claims; author acceptance remains the separate TL-075 gate.

acceptance.given: A search-capable model
then: Enumerable benchmarks, simple-policy/random-search comparisons, response/stress sensitivity and fresh assessments support the declared bounded search claim.

acceptance.given: Full ledger and frozen financial cases
then: Fixture parity remains a financial equivalence check; independent actor/physical validation is still required.

requirements.title: Replay and export a discovered strategy
requirements.statement: A saved search result shall include policy, initial state, objective definition, actor/uncertainty models, model/engine versions, random-stream plan and traceable evaluation artifacts.

acceptance.given: A generated finalist that was not one of the six authored cases
acceptance.when: It is exported and replayed in a fresh supported environment
then: Its selected trajectories and aggregate evaluation reproduce within declared tolerances.
The event timeline identifies Pacifica actions, other actors' actions and chance outcomes separately.
The export can become a new draft narrative/scenario without implying canon approval.
Missing external assets are identified before replay.
Exports include decision-context/reason revisions, immutable observation payloads, predicate/time definitions, conduct bindings, narrative/search status and root/evaluation/branch population lineage.

requirements.title: Score distributions without hiding their assumptions
requirements.statement: Objective evaluation shall support means, quantiles, cumulative/path measures, tail losses and joint threshold attainment with clear probability/weight semantics, horizon treatment and missing-data rules.

acceptance.given: Two policies with close means, sparse tail losses and different survival profiles
then: Metric aggregation, risk statistic, weight/probability status and joint target attainment are explicit.
Sample uncertainty and adaptive sampling needs are shown; unweighted scenario fractions are not historical probabilities.
Financial/physical terminal duties are reported or bounded; unresolved continuation cannot become a winning zero penalty.
Computational failures remain status records and cannot be treated as success, discarded silently or converted to arbitrary utility penalties.

Report declared population membership, denominator unit, selection and weights. A 100-world assessment with 20 unsupported paths and 20 conditional continuations retains 100 parent evaluations, 80 supported/20 unsupported, plus 20 separate conditional child executions; retries and cache reuse are not evidence.

requirements.title: Demonstrate discovery without prewritten outcomes
requirements.statement: R1 shall demonstrate discovery and assessment of new adaptive policies in a bounded domain with independent actors; R0 is a foundation release and six scripted histories cannot satisfy the discovery goal.

acceptance.given: A fixed starting world, catalog, objective/descriptor set and uncertainty design without authored future outcomes
then: At least 1,000 candidate policies and 100,000 generated paths meet the declared benchmark or an explicit revised scope.
Conditional decisions differ after relevant observations; counterparties can refuse/counteroffer and alter later events.
Outputs include an estimated trade-off frontier, per-cell Pareto strategy archive, own-interest response analysis and separately labelled hostile stress tests.
Held-out assessments, history types and replayable terminal failures support the bounded claim; no automatic exploit label follows merely from lost advantage.
The R1 demonstration includes bounded narrative-condition search and an author usefulness review; rollout volume alone does not satisfy plot discovery.

requirements.title: Gate metrics on usable evidence and coverage
requirements.statement: Every displayed or scored state/success measure shall identify definition, scale, boundary, sources/assumptions, module coverage and uncertainty from R0; unsupported claims shall be unavailable or explicitly labelled conditional proxies.

acceptance.given: A readiness, prosperity or human-cost measure with missing mechanism or population coverage
acceptance.when: A sketch or campaign tries to enable it
then: The missing mechanism/data/denominator is visible before display or ranking.
Physical, behavioral and qualitative/ordinal evidence remain distinguishable; invented precise scores are rejected.
Named proxies retain their own labels and limits; source categories do not imply Pacifica calibration.
Campaign objectives must additionally meet TL-041 before optimization.

A material mechanism leaving its applicability envelope propagates an unsupported or conditional status to dependent claims; rejected statistical recommendations may remain inspectable as explicitly provisional story experiments.

requirements.title: Sketch interactively
requirements.statement: Editing a supported R0 lever shall evaluate the bounded policy without search, stream progressive outcome fans and compare with a pinned reference under matched exogenous worlds; only the declared narrow controls are required initially.

acceptance.given: A saved bounded financing/commitment sketch on the reference hardware
acceptance.when: The author changes a supported term or threshold
then: Current-identity distributions display 1,000 paths within the provisional 1-second p95 target and 10,000 within 10 seconds, subject to the M0 decision.
The view shows sample count, uncertainty/coverage, partial/complete status and calibration/reference-check labels.
A new edit supersedes work without publishing stale chunks as current; only owned native jobs are cancelled.
A selected path opens an offline structured timeline and deterministic summary, and an explicit save creates a named version; no LLM narration or general catalog editor is needed for R0.

requirements.title: Simulate on an explicit compiled layout
requirements.statement: The fast engine shall advance many worlds on a versioned fixed-shape layout with explicit state bindings and isolation; compiled per-world kernels are allowed when profiling favors them, while repeated interpreted Python dispatch is kept out of the hot path.

acceptance.given: A realistic layout and branch-heavy policy/actor/action queue with checks and logging
acceptance.when: Single, batched and partitioned executions are profiled
then: Draws, event decisions and numeric results satisfy TL-011/TL-047 and information-boundary tests.
Each field binding declares units, indexing, initialization and update ownership; activation masks and queue/capacity overflow have explicit failure behavior rather than truncation.
Profiling reports resolution/compilation, modules, response/queue logic, summaries, persistence and delivery with peak memory.
NumPy batching and Numba kernels are compared on actual data; no rule requires every branch to be forced into array masks.

requirements.title: Validate the fast model on baseline and changed cases
requirements.statement: The fast model shall fit declared aggregate baseline series within pinned calibration bands and pass independent changed-input reference cases for the bounded claim; baseline fitting alone is insufficient.

acceptance.given: Baseline core nominal/real GDP, revenue, expenditure, debt and cash plus small independently calculated financing/commitment examples
then: Reports state source hashes, price/perimeter, year, band and residual; calibration never claims fixture parity or historical validation.
Independent cases include accepted/refused/counteroffered credit, changed interest/maturity/draw dates, failed rollover and interim liquidity shortage with later feasibility effects.
Reference expectations use separately derived calculations or enumerated cases, not copied fast-engine outputs.

Accounting numeric tolerances, baseline bands and off-baseline fidelity/decision discrepancy rules are separate and versioned; a changed feasible action or loss state is material regardless of an aggregate band.

requirements.title: Check paths and re-evaluate policies with the detailed ledger
requirements.statement: Detailed-ledger assessment shall support immutable forensic checking of a recorded history and separate policy re-evaluation under detailed states, using shared mechanism definitions and explicit fidelity projections rather than independently invented economics.

acceptance.given: A generated non-fixture path whose detailed timing reveals a financing shortage
then: Forensic mode checks recorded decisions and flags the first impossible commitment or financial discrepancy; it does not force acceptance, supply money or claim subsequent decisions remain feasible.
Policy mode reruns the same conditional policy and exogenous-world design under detailed observations/resources; actor responses and later choices may differ, producing a new linked trajectory.
Full instrument postings, decimal rounding, cash/claims schedules, input versions and mode lineage are inspectable.
A decision/feasibility reversal triggers reassessment even inside a broad calibration band; metric discrepancies use their own assessed fidelity rules.
Promoting or reranking policies requires sufficient consistently assessed finalists; fast and detailed values never mix silently, and unsupported detailed coverage remains provisional.

requirements.title: Map diverse strategies without forced scalar quality
requirements.statement: The strategy map shall retain a bounded nondominated policy set within each author-chosen behavior cell, with explicit descriptor aggregation, uncertainty, capacity and deterministic pruning rules alongside the global Pareto set.

acceptance.given: A small enumerable multiobjective policy family and behavior descriptors varying across futures
acceptance.when: The archive is built and repeated
then: With sufficient cell capacity, each cell's nondominated set agrees with exhaustive evaluation; bounded pruning matches the declared deterministic rule.
No hidden weighted score selects a single best policy; the UI exposes within-cell trade-offs and assessment status.
Descriptor coordinates use a registered summary over a common world design, including never/undefined cases, sample uncertainty and cell instability; a lucky realized path cannot assign policy type.
Coverage or a different behavior cell is not evidence of robustness; later response and fresh assessment results remain separate.
The author story archive persists independently of global/per-cell pruning and is not scored as a strategy archive.
Strategic archive pruning cannot prevent candidate extraction from a history; novel conflict/choice structures can remain accessible even when their generating policy is dominated in every cell.

requirements.title: Separate own-interest responses from hostile stress tests
requirements.statement: Finalists shall face bounded best/near-best response analysis under each actor's own declared preferences, information and resources, plus a separately labelled hostile stress search with explicit plausibility and acceptable-own-outcome bounds.

acceptance.given: A cooperative counterparty, a competing actor and a deliberately defective opponent model
acceptance.when: Response and stress searches and at least one Pacifica revision round run
then: Ordinary response analysis uses the actor's own utility or documented preference procedure; cooperation is allowed and harmful-to-Pacifica is not an assumed objective.
Stress analysis states which Pacifica outcome is stressed, actor interests/near-best tolerances, capabilities, information, hostility assumptions and budget.

Rank changes or lost advantage are labelled response/stress sensitivity; an exploit finding requires a reproducible violation, unrealistic mechanism or documented model defect, not merely a stronger reply.
The seeded defect is demonstrated by a counterexample/reference check; one round is not presented as equilibrium or a guarantee of low exploitability.
All response models and revised Pacifica candidates are frozen before final held-out assessment.

Response searches use declared actor knowledge of Pacifica's policy, not hidden policy code by default; joint versus unilateral response assumptions and incompatible combinations of replies are explicit.

requirements.title: Group histories into inspectable types
requirements.statement: Rollouts shall be grouped using registered event/trajectory features into history types with empirical shares, distinguishing associations and representative paths, preserving rare and terminal outcomes.

acceptance.given: A policy's assessed histories including outliers, terminal losses and computational errors
then: Feature scaling, clustering and scenario-discovery methods/parameters are versioned; representative paths are actual members.
Shares are fractions of the stated tested ensemble unless probability calibration is justified; distinguishing conditions remain associations.
Rare/outlier and terminal paths remain inspectable even if not in a large cluster; computational errors retain separate status and are not fabricated histories.
Type labels and representatives link to replayable events, counts, coverage and model assumptions.
Author annotations and saved interesting paths survive cluster reassignment; selected narratives do not change empirical cluster shares.

Narrative causal signatures use supported actor goals, conflicting/frustrated plans, consequential choices and information changes; numerical jitter does not establish a new plot. Statistical history clusters and narrative candidate diversity are separate views.

requirements.title: Narrate recorded facts with bounded claims
requirements.statement: Optional LLM narration shall render a selected structured history after calculation using a typed claim record and inserted result values; R0 shall remain fully usable with deterministic templates and the timeline.

acceptance.given: A recorded path and a proposed synopsis with a correct number but an invented motive or causal explanation
then: Each consequential event/actor/time and asserted motive or causal relation needs explicit supporting records; unsupported claims are rejected or clearly separated as author speculation.
Numeric placeholders insert saved values; ID/number matching alone is not described as semantic truth verification.
A structured claim/template boundary is authoritative; ambiguous free prose requires review rather than an absolute automated grounding guarantee.
Provider/prompt/model, claim references and checks are saved; narration is draft/non-canon, optional and unable to change results; offline use remains complete.

Optional LLM prose follows the R0 author usefulness gate; deterministic summaries remain complete in R0/R1. Goal and belief records can ground motives, but do not establish historical or canonical truth.

Motive claims cite a DecisionRecord and inputs actually used by its procedure, not merely an attached Goal or a retrospective author rationale; dramatic relations retain their derivation and evidence status.

requirements.title: Generate structural schemas with explicit runtime bindings
requirements.statement: Shared typed declarations shall generate supported structural artifacts such as catalog/exchange schemas, result schemas and form/layout metadata; simulation semantics, runtime mappings, migrations and interaction design remain explicit reviewed code.

acceptance.given: An added descriptive field and a new state-changing field
then: Supported structural artifacts regenerate and CI detects drift.
Descriptive metadata cannot silently become numeric state; a state field requires declared units, initialization, index binding, update rule, migration and tests before execution.
Generated form scaffolds do not supply policy semantics or approval workflows.
Each run pins declaration, schema, layout and mapping versions; R0 can use minimal typed schemas and hand-written bindings without a universal generator.
R0/R1 use explicit minimal schemas and bindings for the bounded ontology; broad generation follows the demonstrated author workflow.

requirements.title: Store batched results with recoverable manifests
requirements.statement: Outcomes and selected trajectories shall be written in batches as immutable content-addressed columnar artifacts, with retained manifests and a rebuildable local query catalog; time steps shall not write rows individually.

acceptance.given: A 100,000-rollout artifact set and interruption between file publication and index registration
then: Compact summaries meet the provisional query target on declared workload/hardware; storage and query time are measured separately.
A single catalog coordinator registers only durable completed artifacts; an atomic rename alone is not claimed to transact across files, Git and DuckDB.
Retained run manifests rebuild the index; incomplete/orphan files cannot appear as complete results.
Nonstored details replay in the pinned environment and reconcile to saved summaries; coverage and error counts survive recovery.

Persist candidate-selection configuration, coverage/eviction and reconstructible references before strategic pruning; MetricSample tables remain distinct from delivered Observation records and population membership survives recovery.

requirements.title: Define and enforce world semantics
requirements.statement: Supported records shall enforce registered predicate signatures, state keys and ownership, immutable revisions, target/valid/belief/receipt times, qualified relationships and branch scope, with machine-checkable invariants for the active ontology subset.

acceptance.given: A bounded world with conflicting source assertions, an unknown consent state, an officeholder change and inherited obligations
acceptance.when: The resolver validates and compiles its active ontology subset
then: Distinct people, offices, institutions and factions retain stable IDs and dated roles; succession follows an explicit asset/obligation mapping.
Unknown, absent, refused and disputed consent remain distinct. Source assertions and public statements cannot silently overwrite branch truth or actor beliefs.
Qualified rights and obligations name all parties, subject matter, conditions, dates and authority; a country-level Boolean cannot replace the agreement.
Record contracts and invariant IDs agree with ontology.md and the structured catalog; unsupported record effects fail before execution.
